svg.text: Lifeboat stations: the folding guard at the deck's open edge · JS4-413 · revision 0 · 13 November 2026

Boat deck, port and starboard (the starboard station is the mirror image). Drawn before it is built. The station itself, its davits, boat and end rails are as built (blender/fittings_boats.py); the guard is new.
Seen from inboard: the sea is behind the sheet. 7.6 m of edge are open between the inner posts of the station's end rails, about 10 m over the water. Heights over the deck.
the boat, stowed: her keel 1.40 m over the deck
Port station, looking forward: outboard is to the right. The guard up (full) and folded (dashed); the boat stowed, and her keel's way out.
her keel passes the guard's line
out of 46: the guard stands 1.03 m
· It stands, as drawn, whenever the boat is stowed: nobody walks off the open edge under
· Before the boat is swung out: the four snap hooks off the end posts' eyes, the three
locking pins out, and the stanchions fold inboard flat on the deck with their chains, each
head on its pad. On the page: a tap on the guard, at either station.
· THE DAVITS ARE NOT TURNED OUT WHILE THE GUARD STANDS: her keel would strike it (0.96 m
against 1.03 m). The page refuses the order and says why.
· THE GUARD IS NOT RAISED WHILE THE DAVITS ARE OUT. When the boat is home and the davits are
stowed, a tap raises it again: pins in, hooks on.
· The gaps in the rail at the liferafts' cradles (1.7 m each) are sheet 2: chains under each
· No scantling is calculated. Chain, hooks and pins are the yard's choice; the rule behind a
guard's height and openings is as the yard's reference has it, not read again.
· Folded, the chains lie as stiff as they hung: the model's parts are rigid.
34 mm tube, 1.03 m high, a boss on its hinge pin, an eye for each chain toward each neighbour. They stand 1.90 m apart on the end rails' own line
A base plate 110 by 120 mm welded to the deck, two cheeks 140 mm high, the hinge pin 35 mm over the deck
Through both cheeks and the stanchion, 105 mm over the deck: red, with a ring, on a lanyard to the base plate. It holds the stanchion upright
8 mm galvanised chain at 1.00 and 0.62 m, the heights of the rail's top and middle courses, in four bays; it hangs 30 mm in the middle of a bay
Each chain ends in a snap hook, hooked into an eye welded to the end rail's inner post under its rail course
Rubber, 18 mm high, 0.93 m inboard of the hinge: a folded stanchion's head lies on it, clear of the davit frames
Made by ferry/yard/drawings/guard_drawing.py from ferry/blender/guard_place.py: the numbers the guard is built from.
